title: soft-handoff prefill coordinator with confidence feedback loops
creator: Anjali Rao
description: Implement a soft-handoff prefill coordinator that enables speculative decoding with an explicit confidence feedback loop between prefill probes and decode commit logic. The coordinator should be kernel-aware (use kernel-fit signals and latency budgets) and support staged token commit thresholds so that early outputs can be surfaced when acceptance metrics are high while enabling graceful fallbacks when probes indicate low confidence. This ticket covers design, runtime API changes, telemetry, rollout plan, and tests needed for a safe canary deployment.
acceptance_criteria: Coordinator adds <5% p50 latency overhead for prefill path on typical benchmarks
Early-accept delta (EAD) metric implemented and emitted as a first-class telemetry field
Graceful fallback path triggers and falls back to conservative decode variant within configured SLA 99th percentile
End-to-end e2e tests for acceptance thresholds, rollback behavior, and kernel-affinity toggles in CI
Canary rollout to 5% production traffic with auto-rollback on defined regression signals
implementation_notes: Introduce a lightweight PreFillCoordinator component in the runtime dispatcher responsible for: probe dispatch, confidence scoring, and handoff decisioning
Confidence scoring will combine probe logits delta, KV hit-stability, and a new kernel-fit score (0..1) computed from historic per-kernel latency residuals
Expose a pluggable acceptance function: accepts inputs {probe_score, kernel_fit, latency_budget, request_priority} and returns an acceptance_score and suggested fallback variant

Add a soft-handoff commit model: partial token commit when acceptance_score > commit_high, conservative commit when acceptance_score between commit_low and commit_high, full fallback when < commit_low
Make kernel-fit score observable and cache it per model+sequence-length bucket to reduce compute
Integrate with routing layer: coordinator returns routing hint to runtime router for immediate fallback model selection if acceptance fails
Minimal runtime API changes: add CoordinatorSignals in per-request metadata and a short-lived probe trace id for correlation
testing_and_rollout: Unit tests for acceptance function with synthetic probe signals and deterministic kernel-fit inputs
Integration test harness that simulates mixed traffic (short chat bursts, long completion workloads) and verifies fallback latency and cost behavior
Load test with bursty prefill profiles to validate autoscale interactions and ensure coordinator doesn't become a hot path
Canary rollout plan: 0% -> 1% -> 5% -> 20% with health gates on EAD regressions, 95/99 latency SLOs, and model quality deltas
Run offline simulation over last 30 days of production traces to compute expected commit regret vs cost savings trade-offs
telemetry_metrics: commit_regret_rate (cases where partial commit later rolled back)
open_questions: What are safe defaults for commit_low and commit_high across tiers (dev/standard/premium)?
Should kernel-fit score be warmed from offline profiling or learned online with decay?
How to quantify commit_regret cost in dollars for ops-level rollout gating?
Is there any privacy/telemetry concern from emitting per-request kernel identifiers to central metrics?
How to coordinate with Dedicated capacity routing policies when fallback implies a different capacity tier?
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Coordinator adds contention on dispatcher path -> Mitigation: offload heavy scoring to a bounded worker pool and cache recent decisions
Risk: Early partial commits cause incoherent user-visible outputs -> Mitigation: conservatively threshold commit_high and add roll-forward-only path for short sessions
Risk: Mis-calibrated acceptance causes excessive fallbacks increasing cost -> Mitigation: simulation and small canary, gating on fallback.activation_rate budget
Risk: Kernel-fit estimation drifts on new hardware -> Mitigation: periodic re-profiling job and per-region kernel-fit overrides
notes: This ticket intentionally separates decisioning from kernel selection; coordinator returns hints rather than forcing kernel swaps to keep the change incremental
Leaning on existing probe machinery but adding a small probe metadata envelope for richer signals
We should plan a short spike (2d) to prototype online kernel-fit computation and impact on p95 before full implementation
